definition: Adding a term rewarding high policy entropy to the RL objective, the standard remedy for collapse inherited from classical RL. Every empirical source that tests it here reports it working poorly for language models: highly sensitive to its coefficient, prone to uncontrolled entropy growth after a few hundred steps together with a jump in response length, and able to dominate the advantage signal because it is optimized independently of it. The archive now holds the reason as well as the observation. One source proves the bonus modifies the stationary condition, so training converges somewhere other than the reward optimum and the shortfall is at least the coefficient times an entropy gap — non-zero whenever the true optimum is not itself the maximum-entropy one, which is the usual case where answers are near-deterministic. The same source shows it shrinks the stability margin, and that annealing the coefficient to zero is what restores unbiasedness. A second theoretical entry runs the other way, treating a fixed positive regularizer as the objective and proving policy gradient converges to *its* optimum exponentially fast — a reminder that the term is a choice about what to optimize and not only a stabilizer.

evidence.note: Establishes that RL trades policy entropy for reward along a predictable exponential curve R = -a·exp(H) + b, derives that entropy change is driven by the covariance between action probability and advantage, and controls it by restricting updates to the highest-covariance tokens.
evidence.title: The Entropy Mechanism of Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning Language Models

evidence.note: Reduces the question of whether an update raises or lowers entropy to the sign of one scalar per token, shows that under GRPO what matters is that scalar's deviation from a policy-weighted baseline rather than its own value, and proves the deviation averages to zero over a batch.
evidence.title: On the Entropy Dynamics in Reinforcement Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models

evidence.note: Recasts entropy collapse as an imbalance of 'entropy flow' — tokens whose update lowers entropy persistently outweigh those that raise it — and rebalances the two sets with a closed-form coefficient computed from each batch, without reference policies or entropy bonuses.
evidence.title: Understanding and Preventing Entropy Collapse in RLVR with On-Policy Entropy Flow Optimization

evidence.note: A systematic empirical study of entropy in RLVR that finds entropy correlates with response diversity but only weakly and inconsistently with accuracy, identifies clipping thresholds, off-policy updates and data diversity as its drivers, and argues positive-advantage tokens are what collapses it.
evidence.title: Revisiting Entropy in Reinforcement Learning for Large Reasoning Models

evidence.note: Proves that entropy-regularized policy gradient converges to the regularized optimum at an exponential rate for log-linear softmax policies over continuous state and action spaces, by using the KL regularizer as a Lyapunov function to keep the Fisher information matrix from degenerating.
evidence.title: Global linear convergence of entropy-regularized softmax policy gradient beyond tabular MDPs

evidence.note: Proves that an entropy bonus permanently moves the stationary point of RL training while covariance-targeted control reaches the unregularized optimum once its coefficient is annealed, and that the bonus shrinks the stability margin where the targeted methods leave it intact.
evidence.title: A Comparative Theoretical Analysis of Entropy Control Methods in Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning Language Models

name: entropy regularization
